title: Affine comparison of an ideal-product intersection inclusion
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], F and G quasi-coherent O_X-modules [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], g:G \to F a monomorphism, I a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], U an affine open of X, and m,n nonnegative integers. Products and powers are the multiplication images and recursive powers of [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. Suppose I(U)^m F(U) \cap \operatorname{image}(g(U)) is contained in g(U)(I(U)^n G(U)). Then for every open W contained in U, the intersection of the section ranges of I^m F \to F and G \to F is contained in the section range of I^n G \to G \to F. There is no Noetherian, coherence, finiteness or existence-of-a-bound hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 01YA, affine reduction in the proof; Tags 01I8 and 01IC, tensor and exact affine sheaf comparison

proof.text: Prove quasi-coherence of an affine pushforward directly by the two principal-open localization conditions: preimages of basic opens are basic opens, and restriction scalars act via the section-ring map. For the closed subscheme defined by I this gives quasi-coherence of the pushed-forward structure module. Thus I.toModules, its kernel, is quasi-coherent. Tensor products and multiplication images are quasi-coherent by the tensor and image statements. Induct on the recursive power: zero is the unit sheaf, one is I, and subsequent powers are multiplication images. On affine sections the tensor comparison and affine image formula give range equal to the ideal multiple. Starting with range(I.toModules inclusion)=I(U), induction and range_comp give the power range I(U)^r. Applying the same multiplication calculation gives range(I^r M inclusion)=I(U)^r M(U), including r=0.

Form the pullback of I^m F -> F and G -> F. Its section range in F is the intersection of the two section ranges because evaluation preserves pullbacks. It is quasi-coherent: identify the pullback with the kernel of the map from the binary direct sum to F, given by the first inclusion minus g.

Use the assumed submodule inclusion and the affine power-product range calculation to lift the image of every affine section of this pullback through I^n G -> F. Explicitly the inclusion supplies a section t in I(U)^n G(U); the range formula supplies its preimage b in I^n G(U), and composing b with g gives the original section.

For a morphism from a quasi-coherent module vanishing on U, cover any W <= U by basic opens D(f). A section on D(f) becomes the restriction of a section on U after multiplication by f^k. Naturality makes f^k times its image zero. Since f is a unit on D(f), its image is zero. Sheaf separatedness then gives vanishing on W. Apply this to the pullback inclusion composed with the cokernel of the mono I^n G -> F.

The kernel of this cokernel is the Abelian image. Since I^n G -> F is mono, its factorization through that image is an isomorphism. Applying its inverse to the kernel-section lift gives a section of I^n G over W mapping to the original section. Combine with the pullback section-range equality to obtain the required inclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem affine_ideal_intersection_inclusion {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (F G : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (g : G ⟶ F) [Mono g] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (U : X.affineOpens) (m n : ℕ)
    (hmodule : I.ideal U ^ m • (⊤ : Submodule Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1)) ⊓
        LinearMap.range (g.val.app (.op U.1)).hom ≤
      Submodule.map (g.val.app (.op U.1)).hom
        (I.ideal U ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule Γ(X, U.1) Γ(G, U.1)))) :
    ∀ W : X.Opens, W ≤ U.1 →
      Set.range ((idealModuleProductι (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).2 F).app W) ∩
          Set.range (g.app W) ⊆
        Set.range ((idealModuleProductι (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).2 G ≫ g).app W)
